findings.problem: Orchestrator decisions 15 and 21 assign the schema corrections discovered while drafting to the G2 fixers because 9999_init.sql is unfrozen until 2.4 pastes it. None of them is in the 1.2 table list: the archival columns on profiles (`archived_at timestamptz`, `archived_by uuid`, `archive_reason text check in ('user','deletion_request','admin')`), `account_deletion_requests.scheduled_for timestamptz` (decision 15, constant ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30 documented next to the default), `bulletins.publish_at` / `documents.publish_at` explicitly nullable (decision 21), and `calendars.members_can_submit boolean not null default true` (decision 21, G12 gap). Without them 6.3a has to ship a 9996 migration and 5.3 cannot honour the calendar flag.
findings.fix: In Build 7 (3): add `archived_at timestamptz, archived_by uuid, archive_reason text check (archive_reason in ('user','deletion_request','admin'))` to `profiles`; change `account_deletion_requests` to `(user_id pk fk auth.users cascade, requested_at default now(), scheduled_for timestamptz not null default now() + interval '30 days' -- ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30 (orchestrator decision 15), processed_at)`; write `publish_at timestamptz null default now()` for `bulletins` and `documents` with a comment 'null = draft'; add `members_can_submit boolean not null default true` to `calendars`. Add to Inputs: 'Orchestrator decisions 15 and 21: the account-archival columns and the Phase 2 corrections live in 9999 because it is not yet pasted.' Add the same names to G2 open_issues so G3 (1.4 policies/tests) and G14 (6.3a) reuse them.

findings.quote: decision 7 keeps `trial_ends_at` (set to now()+30 days by the super-admin UI, not by a column default)
findings.problem: Skeleton founder decision 7 says '`trial_ends_at` default now()+30d on church creation'; the prompt turns that into an assertion that there is deliberately no column default, which is the drafter's interpretation, not the founder's decision, and leaves the 30-day trial dependent on UI code (2.2) alone.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'decision 7: `trial_ends_at` defaults to now() + 30 days on church creation — give the column `default now() + interval ''30 days''` (DESIGN §4.2 shows no default; record the addition under Deviations from plan) so the trial exists even when a church is created by SQL; 2.2 may still show/override it.'

findings.problem: Orchestrator decisions 15 and 21 route several trigger/helper corrections into 1.3a via the G2 fixers, none of which appear: (a) decision 15 — the `app.*` membership helpers (`member_org_ids`, `perm_org_ids`, `my_household_ids`, `fellowship_visible_org_ids`) must treat users with `profiles.archived_at is not null` as non-members (no org reads, no push, excluded from directory and audiences); (b) decision 21 / G9 — `app.on_content_publish` must move the existing queued notification's `scheduled_for` when `publish_at` changes instead of only inserting when none exists; (c) decision 21 / G12 — `app.force_event_pending` must honour `organization_settings.events_require_approval` (auto-approve when false) and the new `calendars.members_can_submit`; (d) decision 21 / G13 — `app.guard_system_audience_groups` trigger (system rows: no rename/delete/kind change; custom only via permission).
findings.fix: Add to Build 2: 'Every helper that derives membership joins `public.profiles` and excludes rows where `archived_at is not null` (orchestrator decision 15) — an archived user is a non-member everywhere.' In Build 3 change `on_content_publish` to: 'when a queued (not claimed/sent) notification already exists for (kind, ref_id) and `publish_at`/`opens_at` changed, update its `scheduled_for` instead of inserting'. Change `force_event_pending` to: 'unless the caller has `announcements.create` or is super admin: set `submitted_by`, and set `status = ''pending''`, `push = false` only when `organization_settings.events_require_approval` is true (else `approved`, `push = false`); raise `calendar_submissions_closed` (42501) when the calendar''s `members_can_submit` is false'. Add `app.guard_system_audience_groups()` (before update or delete on `audience_groups`: rows with `kind <> ''custom''` may not be deleted or have `kind`/`name` changed → `system_group_immutable` P0001) with trigger `audience_groups_guard_system_audience_groups`. Add these names to open_issues and the SQLSTATE catalogue in 1.3b.

findings.problem: The Goal and Build sections name 25 helpers (17 in Build 1 plus my_person_id, can_edit_household, person_in_kind, person_in_group, user_in_group, can_read_object, can_write_object, rate_limit_hit), not 24; and done_when says 'the 24 helper signatures match DESIGN §4.4's grant list exactly' while that grant list (`grant execute … to authenticated`) has 18 entries. The wrong numbers make the agent hunt for a missing helper or drop one.
findings.fix: Verify: '→ at least 42 (25 helpers + 17 trigger functions)'. done_when[1]: 'Schema `app` contains at least 42 functions, every one `security definer` with `search_path` in `proconfig`; the 18 helper signatures in DESIGN §4.4''s authenticated grant list match exactly (e.g. …)'. Goal: replace 'every `app.*` helper from PLAN §4' with 'all 25 `app.*` helpers'.

findings.quote: copy from DESIGN §4.4 verbatim: … `app.require_writable(org uuid)` (raises `organization_suspended`, errcode `42501`), `app.require_user()` (raises `auth_required`, `42501`)
findings.problem: DESIGN's bodies raise 'organization is suspended' and 'authentication required' (human text); the repo convention adopted here puts the snake_case key in `message`. 'Verbatim' and the convention contradict each other for these two functions, and the agent must guess which wins.
findings.fix: Change to 'copy from DESIGN §4.4 verbatim EXCEPT the raise statements, which follow the repo convention below (message = snake_case key, human text moves to `detail`) — record this as a deliberate deviation in the section (5) comment block'.

findings.problem: DESIGN §4.2 says `pg_trigger_depth() > 0`. The prompt's `> 1` is actually the correct intent (inside the guard itself depth is already 1, so `> 0` would always skip), but the prompt neither says it deviates nor why, so a careful agent following 'DESIGN is authoritative' may revert it.
findings.fix: Append: '(DESIGN §4.2 writes `> 0`, which would always be true inside the trigger; use `> 1` — i.e. skip only when fired by a cascade from another trigger — and note the correction under Deviations from plan).'

findings.quote: named `<table>_<function>` (for example `organizations_on_org_created`, `households_guard_privacy`, `announcements_on_content_publish`), including the two on `auth.users` (`auth_users_on_created`, `auth_users_on_updated`)
findings.problem: Two of the examples break the stated rule: `<table>_<function>` gives `households_guard_household_privacy_columns` and `auth_users_on_auth_user_created` / `auth_users_on_auth_user_updated`. G2's open_issues tells G3 that 07_storage_billing_audit tests assert on these names, so the rule and the examples must agree.
findings.fix: Either state the rule as '`<table>_<short name>` where the short name drops the `guard_`/`on_` prefix noise, and list every trigger name explicitly', or fix the examples to `households_guard_household_privacy_columns`, `auth_users_on_auth_user_created`, `auth_users_on_auth_user_updated`. Then copy the final list into open_issues for G3.

findings.quote: Write: a row exists whose `storage_path`/`photo_path` EQUALS `name` exactly and the caller holds the matching permission (`sermons.upload`, `bulletins.upload`, `documents.upload`, `org.settings` for `org-assets`
findings.problem: For the `org-assets` bucket the matching column is `organization_settings.logo_path` (DESIGN §4.2, §7 path `{org_id}/logo/{uuid}.png`), which is neither `storage_path` nor `photo_path`; the prompt never names it, so the agent may invent a column or skip the exact-path rule for logos.
findings.fix: Change to: '… whose `storage_path` (`sermons`/`bulletins`/`documents`), `photo_path` (`households`/`persons`) or `organization_settings.logo_path` (`org-assets`) EQUALS `name` exactly …'.

findings.quote: `srv_process_account_deletions() returns int`: for each unprocessed `account_deletion_requests` row: `set local app.cascade = 'on'` … `request_account_deletion() returns void` (client): `require_user()`; upsert the request row for `auth.uid()`.
findings.problem: Orchestrator decision 15 (founder, 2026-09-07) changes both RPCs and adds three more, and its 'Schema home' paragraph puts them in 1.3b because 9999 is unpasted: `request_account_deletion()` must archive the account immediately (reason `deletion_request`, push devices deleted) and set `scheduled_for = requested_at + 30 days`; `srv_process_account_deletions()` processes only rows whose `scheduled_for` has passed; new client RPC `deactivate_account()` and service RPCs `srv_archive_account(user_id, reason)` / `srv_restore_account(user_id)` (restore returns memberships, permissions and directory visibility). Decision 21 also adds `srv_load_unlocked_share_link(link_id)` (G8), atomic `set_head_of_house` (G12), and changes `srv_claim_notifications` to `(org_id, max_rows)` (G9). The prompt's 'exactly 24 functions' verify count and 'Signatures are frozen … do not add parameters' constraint both contradict these decisions.
findings.fix: Add Build items: '17. `deactivate_account() returns void`: `require_user()`; set `profiles.archived_at = now(), archived_by = auth.uid(), archive_reason = ''user''`; delete the user''s `push_devices`. 18. `srv_archive_account(user_id uuid, reason text) returns void` (same effect, reason from the argument, `archived_by` = null for the cron); `srv_restore_account(user_id uuid) returns void` clears the three columns and deletes any pending `account_deletion_requests` row. 19. `srv_load_unlocked_share_link(link_id uuid) returns jsonb` — returns the same `ok` payload as `srv_resolve_share_link` for a link already unlocked by cookie, without password or rate-limit checks (decision 21; name flagged). 20. `set_head_of_house(person_id uuid) returns void` — directory admin or household adult; in one statement demote the current `head` to `spouse`/`other` and promote the person (orchestrator decision 6 index).' Rewrite item 14: `request_account_deletion()` calls the archive logic with reason `deletion_request` and inserts the request with `scheduled_for = now() + interval ''30 days''` (ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30); `srv_process_account_deletions()` processes only `processed_at is null and scheduled_for <= now()`. Rewrite item 12 to `srv_claim_notifications(org_id uuid, max_rows int)` (null org_id = all orgs). Update Goal/Verify counts to 21 client + 10 srv = 31 functions, the signature examples, done_when[1], the error catalogue (`account_archived` 42501 raised by `require_user` when the caller is archived), and the Constraints sentence to 'Signatures are frozen by DESIGN §4.4''s grant lists plus the additions in orchestrator decisions 15 and 21'.

findings.quote: `srv_audience_user_ids(group_id uuid, org uuid) returns setof uuid`
findings.problem: PLAN §4 and DESIGN §4.3 write `srv_audience_user_ids(group, org)`, and G9 (3.6) and G13 (5.5) repeat `srv_audience_user_ids(group, org)`. Because PostgREST `rpc()` passes arguments by name, the parameter names in 9999 are part of the contract that 1.7's `rpc.ts`, 3.6 and 5.5 must use; `group` is a reserved word so `group_id` is the right choice, but the prompt does not say it deviates from the docs or record the final parameter names anywhere.
findings.fix: Append to item 10: '(the docs write `group`; it is a reserved word, so the parameter is `group_id` — record this under Deviations from plan)'. Add to Finish/HANDOFF and to G2 open_issues: 'Parameter names of every RPC (PostgREST passes them by name): list them verbatim so 1.7 `rpc.ts`, 3.2, 3.4, 3.6 and 5.5 call `rpc(''srv_audience_user_ids'', { group_id, org })` etc.'

findings.quote: `share_link_invalid P0001`, `share_link_revoked P0001`, `share_link_expired P0001`, `share_link_max_views P0001`, `share_link_rate_limited P0001`, `share_link_wrong_password P0001` … `srv_resolve_share_link` never raises for expected outcomes — it returns a status (see 9).
findings.problem: The catalogue lists six `share_link_*` keys as raised errors, but item 9 (and DESIGN §4.4) says the only function that could raise them returns statuses instead, so no function raises them; the catalogue format 'raised by <functions>' cannot be filled and `errors.ts` (1.6) would map keys that never occur.
findings.fix: Remove the six `share_link_*` keys from the raised-error catalogue and add a second comment block 'Status strings returned by `srv_resolve_share_link` (not errors): ok, invalid, revoked, expired, max_views, sharing_disabled, unpublished, needs_password_reset, needs_password, wrong_password, rate_limited', which 1.6 also mirrors.

findings.quote: Add section (5c) "RPCs" to `9999_init.sql`, physically after section (7) (RPCs reference the views and the triggers must exist for the smoke checks; plpgsql bodies are not validated at creation time anyway).
findings.problem: PLAN §4 'Migration skeleton' and DESIGN §4.4 fix the order (5) functions → (6) views → (7) triggers → (8) policies for every migration, and 1.5's docs/MIGRATIONS.md teaches that order. The justification given is spurious: plpgsql bodies are not validated at creation (so views need not exist first) and smoke checks run after the whole file applies. Placing (5c) after (7) silently breaks the numbered skeleton that later migrations copy.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Add sub-section (5c) "RPCs" inside section (5), after (5b) and before the (6) views header — plpgsql bodies are not validated at creation time, so referencing the views from there is fine. Keep the PLAN §4 order (5) → (6) → (7) intact.'

findings.quote: org not `sermons_shareable` or org not writable → `sharing_disabled`
findings.problem: DESIGN §4.4 'RPC semantics' lists the checks for `srv_resolve_share_link` as link, `revoked_at`, `expires_at`, `max_views`, org `sermons_shareable`, sermon `publish_at` — no organization-status check — and DESIGN §5 / founder decision 7 say suspension blocks writes while 'reads stay available'. Treating a suspended org's public share links as disabled is a defensible product choice (non-paying church), but it is an addition to the design that 3.4's 404-state list (revoked, expired, org disabled sharing, unpublished) does not know about.
findings.fix: Either drop 'or org not writable' to match DESIGN, or keep it and add '(deliberate addition: suspended or cancelled churches stop public sharing — record under Deviations from plan and in open_issues so 3.4 shows the same "sharing disabled" page)'.
